$comment: Which parts of the skill's CSS and JS a page gets. The core is always in. A module is in when the page's body has one of its classes, attributes or tags, matches one of its text patterns, or is named in a <!-- basalt:use name --> comment, and when another module needs it (requires). Modules are added in the order listed here, which is the order of the source files' cascade. classes: every class the module's CSS styles (the test checks them against the CSS and against SKILL.md). budget: the most bytes its minified CSS and JS may reach together. budgets: skillMd (SKILL.md, the context an agent pays: never above what it was), core (the CSS and JS of every page). icons: Phosphor names the module's script draws itself. Raised in the first parity PR (the owner's "bring up the parity"): forms (the number-input, search-clear and file-input chrome), disclosure (the native details marker), status (the accent reader and the forced-colours badge border), spinner (a fixed 16px ring), and the new number, range and accent modules. skillMd rose 10555 to 10900 for the new rules (number field, native chrome, the braille rule, the accent). Raised in the second parity PR (popup rows, levels and the segment's pill): segment 1400 to 3700 (the shared sliding pill: its script, 1.5 KB, and its CSS with the pill's two fallbacks), rows 3600 to 4300 (#27's plate-in-a-row geometry, the plate per level, the glide's shared plate and the forced-colours lit row, net of the removed bar), palette 9400 to 11300 (the glide's script, 2.4 KB: it follows the lit row, travels on a pointer, snaps on a key, and fades in place on leaving). The art module (DECISIONS 101 and 104) is the token groups only some pages name, taken out of the core so the core stays under its cap: the chart roles and lengths, the art colours, the aspect ratios and the stage headroom, in both themes (2087 bytes at 2100; it grows only when a token of those groups is added). A page gets it when its body names one of them, a var() in its own style included. The every-module page has no cap of its own (owner, DECISIONS 79): each part is capped, and a page carries only the parts it uses. usage: the most bytes of a module's usage text (src/usage/NAME.md; core.usage for core.md), which compose.mjs --usage prints on demand. It is context an agent pays only for the modules its page uses, so it is capped per part as SKILL.md and the CSS and script are (DECISIONS 79 and 109). Each is set a little above what its text was when the usage moved out of SKILL.md (DECISIONS 109); raising one needs a reason in the PR, and a rise of 40 to 50% is the owner's. textWords: each text pattern said in words, which compose.mjs --usage prints instead of the regular expression (one for each entry of text, in order). builds: modules a module requires whose markup its script writes, so --usage prints a line saying so instead of their usage text (the palette builds its own rows and key chips). The council's clarity check of the usage texts (all three: not yet clear) raised eight caps because the texts gained what an agent had to guess: callout 200 to 700 (the icon and one wrapper div around the title and body as markup, the four status icons, the role React's Callout renders), palette 1100 to 1300 (an item shown whole, keys as an array, keywords), stats 450 to 800 (a snippet of the figures and of the dl), tabs 500 to 650 (the unselected panels), code 250 to 450 (the markup and what each token class means), segment 150 to 300 (a click does not switch it), progress 150 to 350 (the empty span that paints the fill), theme 250 to 400 (leave the button empty), and accent 250 to 300. Topbar went down, 700 to 500, as its build detail was cut. Raised in the usage PR (the council's clarity check): palette 11300 to 11450 (the module grew 11283 to 11448, +165, about 1.5%), for the guard that makes a string `keys` warn and draw no chip instead of throwing in `keys.filter`, which the palette's usage already promised. Round 2 of the clarity check: tabs 650 to 750 (the panel's top space shown in the snippet, and that the script selects a tab on click). Raised in the site-icons and status PR (skill-parity part A, DECISIONS 106 and 107): status 1650 to 1900 (the neutral, pending and running marks, the badge's real border, and the forced-colours disc, net of the red danger word it drops) and its usage 400 to 1000 (every status in words, the word alone, running, forced colours); rows 4300 to 4450 (the profile list's seat rule and the status parts on a lit row) and its usage 300 to 600 (the profile list, with the one mistake: never an empty element for the seat). New: the links module (2671 bytes: the social row, the new-tab arrow's CSS and the script that draws it; budget 2750) and its usage (1746 bytes; cap 1850), which carries the social link, the glyph set, icon only and the new tab. Dropping Regular halves icons.json. Added in the overlay PR (skill-parity-4, batch 7 step 2, DECISIONS 108): the shared plate leaves palette.js for a glide module (the palette, a menu and the notification centre all call it), so the palette's cap went down, 11450 to 9250, and rows 4450 to 3850 (the plate's CSS moved to glide); and the overlay layer comes in as seven modules a page carries only when it uses them, each with its own cap and usage cap set a little above its size: popover (the native popup shell), menu, dialog (the dialog and alert dialog), sheet (on every side, the top one the site header's narrow menu), tooltip, toast and notifications (the centre). skillMd is unchanged in its cap (the eight new index lines fit within it); the core is unchanged in bytes. Added in the figures and charts PR (skill-parity-5, batch 7 step 3, DECISIONS 108): four modules a page carries only when it uses them, each with its own cap and usage cap set a little above its size: meter (React's Meter, CSS only, 2581 bytes), dlist (the description list, CSS only, 1265), terminal (the code block's transcript: its CSS, 3242, and the script that draws the gutter, the copy button and the replay, 4824) and chart (React's TimeChart and ChartGroup: 7313 of CSS and 23262 of script, which port chart.tsx's scale, layout, lane, labels, sentences, keyboard and table; it needs the art tokens, the table and the kbd chips, and a page without a chart carries none of it). Stats grew for the source line (budget 700 to 850, 798 bytes; its usage 800 to 950, 675 to 899 bytes, +33%, under the owner's 40 to 50%). skillMd is unchanged in its cap (four index lines fit within it); the core is unchanged in bytes. Added in the forms and selection PR (skill-parity-6, batch 7 step 4, DECISIONS 108): six modules a page carries only when it uses them, each with its own cap and usage cap set a little above its size: select (React's Select: the native select's closed trigger in every browser and, where `appearance: base-select` is shipped, the styled list with its two-line rows; a small script that says which input lit a row, 7740 bytes before it, choice (Checkbox, Radio, RadioGroup and Switch as styled native inputs; CSS only, with the first-frame rule), choice-card (ChoiceCard; CSS only), toggle (the pressed toggle's plate and check seat on .btn; CSS only), selection (a table's checkbox column: its fixed width and the script that sets aria-selected, the mixed header box and the count) and loops (the page-level hold on every loop with its switch: the held look and the script that stores it). The select's styles left forms, whose budget fell 3650 to 3250. skillMd rose 8621 to the size of its six new index lines, within its cap; the core is unchanged in bytes; compose adds the stored-hold line to the head of a page that has the loops module. Revised in the same PR (the lead's review of the build): the select gains select.js (one row is lit at a time, by whichever of the pointer and the keys moved last), and choice, toggle, selection and loops carry the first-frame rule, so a state a script sets on load (a mixed header box, the stored hold) paints at once with no crossfade. Added in the navigation and layout PR (skill-parity-7, batch 7 step 5, DECISIONS 108): five modules a page carries only when it uses them, each with its own cap and usage cap set a little above its size: glyph (Basalt's core glyphs drawn by name, at rest and selected, from a table the build works out from the drawn set; a page carries only the glyphs it names, and the drawing of a core glyph from data-glyph left the sheet module, which draws none now), nav (React's Nav: the sidebar's, the narrow menu's and More's rows, with the shared hugging pill), topbar-nav (the site header's links, one action and narrow menu, built by script from the bar's markup), app-shell (the shell, its sidebar and rail, and the app header) and tab-bar (the phone tab bar). The topbar module became the site header's bar (React's SiteHeader, DECISIONS 108: 56px with its line inside, the 44 by 44 brand target, the narrow-screen buttons, the derived sticky offset), budget 1600 to 3200 because its rules gained the app header's shared smoke, and its usage 500 to 750 (+50%) for the lockup's markup (the links, action and menu are topbar-nav's usage). Glide 3700 to 3950: the navigation's pill is a shape inside the row that the plate follows (about 200 bytes). The core's usage 2000 to 2100 (+5%): h2 is the Section step, the prose column's measure, and a link already 44px tall needs no margin. skillMd rose 9317 to 9863 for five index lines, under its cap; the core CSS grew 38 bytes (the layout tokens replace raw lengths, the gutter is one derived property, h2, .prose and .lead follow foundations) and the core script is unchanged. A module's media query writes %bp-md%, %bp-lg% or %bp-container% and the build substitutes the breakpoint tokens. Added in the tables and filters PR (skill-parity-8, batch 7 step 6, DECISIONS 108): the existing table module gains React's table additions (DECISIONS 95: the row header, "Not observed", the row density and the scroll hint with its small script), budget 1400 to 3000 (it was 1134 bytes of CSS; it is 2168 of CSS and 693 of script) and its usage 700 to 950 (+36%); and two modules a page carries only when it uses them, each with its own cap and usage cap set a little above its size: still-table (React's Table with `columns`: the fixed layout from a colgroup, the whole header cell as the sort button with its reserved seat, aria-sort, the pinned columns and their divider, the empty row; 4767 of CSS and 3264 of script, budget 8200) and filter (React's MultiSelect and FilterResult: the chips, the trigger and checklist with the search band from ten values, Clear held in place, the one debounced result line, and the narrowing of a table by `data-column`; 8240 of CSS and 7978 of script, budget 16400; it needs the popover, glide, glyph and choice modules). The core is unchanged in bytes. skillMd rose 9863 to 10128 for two index lines and the CaretUpDown icon's name, within its cap. Added in the commands PR (skill-parity-9, batch 7 step 7, DECISIONS 103 and 108): one new module a page carries only when it uses it, command-list (React's CommandList: the command panel set in the page, list plus preview, the push; it extends the palette and needs rows, kbd and glide; 5229 of CSS and 8734 of script, budget 14000, usage 2150). Two-line rows come to the existing modules: rows 3850 to 5350 (the described row's grid and description line, the push's chevron: 1481 bytes of CSS, the same rules React's menu rows carry), palette 9250 to 9900 (its rows are one function the list shares, with the description and the two-tier ranking of title matches over keyword and description matches; +636) and its usage 1300 to 1350, rows' usage 600 to 800, and glide 3950 to 4000 (a host that is idle counts as having no lit row, +54). skillMd rose 10128 to 10259 for one index line, within its cap; the core's CSS grew 24 bytes (.split.aside takes size-list-width in place of its raw 20rem: the same 320px, so no pixel moves) and the core script is unchanged. Added in the art PR (skill-parity-10, batch 7 step 8, DECISIONS 104 and 108): two modules a page carries only when it uses them, each with its own cap and usage cap set a little above its size: stage (React's Stage and PairedArt: full-bleed art under the site header, the pull-up by the sticky offset, the headroom, the paired art that follows the page's theme, and the forced-colours and print rules; CSS only, 1179 bytes) and framed-art (React's FramedArt: the figure, its rim and radius, the reserved box, the placeholder and the failed alt, the caption and credit; 2208 bytes of CSS and the 733-byte script that sets the frame's phase); both need the art tokens. The bar stays smoked over a stage: React clears it only over a stage that passed the headroom test helper, and a page has no test run (DECISIONS 108's note), so the skill builds no clear state. skillMd rose 10259 to 10500 for two index lines, within its cap; the core is unchanged in bytes. The callout gained the status rim in the same PR (DECISIONS 82, D8's status callouts): success, warning and danger draw their border in the status colour at 45% mixed in sRGB over the callout's own level, one solid colour on every side, and CanvasText in forced colours with the icon; the status colour is now one property the icon and the rim read. Its budget rose 900 to 1150 (the module is 1089 bytes, from 792: +297, about 37%); its usage is unchanged. Added in the overlays-and-the-rest PR (skill-parity-11, batch 7 step 9, DECISIONS 90 and 108): the last two parts of D8's part 5, each a module a page carries only when it uses it, with its own cap and usage cap set a little above its size: combobox (React's Combobox: the input with its caret button inside, the popup of the menu's rows with the glide's shared plate and two-line options, the filtering, the keys, the hidden value, the empty message and the check; 4342 of CSS and 6423 of script, budget 10900, usage 2150; it needs forms, popover and glide, and builds the last two) and sparkline (React's Sparkline: the label and latest value, the line, the axis, the empty sentence and the loading line that breathes; 1609 of CSS and 1874 of script, budget 3600, usage 950). The combobox copies the menu's row rules, as the select's list does, because React's Combobox renders MenuItem rows (a 40px hit area, a 36px plate) and the skill's .row is the palette's 44px: it carries no menu script. popover.js gains the combobox popup in the list of popups that keep focus where it is (+21 bytes, within its cap). skillMd rose 10500 to 10724 for two index lines, within its cap; the core is unchanged in bytes. Added in the motion-rules PR (DECISIONS 136 and 139): one module, ambient (a page's one ambient loop: CSS 828 bytes, script 433, budget 1300, usage 800), taken out of loops so the hold's own module grows only by the icon toggle's glyph swap (loops 2000 to 2200, +10%; its usage 1300 to 1650 for the icon form and the new settings-row sentence, +27%); and the chart's entrance (`entrance: true`: the marks' animations, their conditions and the redraw that restarts them at the elapsed time, 23262 to 25299 bytes of script; budget 30700 to 32800, +7%, usage 2500 to 2950, +18%). The core grew by the three tokens (27704 to 27862 bytes of CSS, under its cap). its stage usage gained the ambient art's line (1650 to 1750, +6%). skillMd rose 10724 to the size of the ambient index line, within its cap. Raised again in the motion-rules amendment (DECISIONS 143): chart 32800 to 33800 (script 25299 to 26375 bytes, +4%; +10% over the 30700 it began with) for the glide a new data set makes mid-entrance, print settling it, and `Basalt.pageChange()`; its usage 2950 to 3150 (+26% over the 2500 it began with). Raised in the second motion-rules amendment (DECISIONS 148): chart 33800 to 34400 (script 26375 to 26970 bytes: a line and its markers glide from their drawn geometry, and `beforeprint` settles the entrance; +12% over the 30700 it began with); topbar-nav 6900 to 7500 (+8.7%: the narrow menu's pause row, its CSS and 275 bytes of script, DECISIONS 148 item 2); loops usage 1650 to 1800 (+38% over the 1300 it began with, for the icon form's `title` and the menu row). Raised in the audit-design-b PR (DECISIONS 138 and 139): still-table 8200 to 13400 (+63%: the module was 7927 bytes and is 13311; the cut cell's plate, its focus stops and its dismissal, ported from React's cell-peek.ts, are 4273 bytes of script and 1111 of CSS; a still table that truncates needs them). The same PR: core usage 2100 to 2250 (+7%: the skip link, one bullet), forms usage 350 to 480 (+37%: the required mark), still-table usage 1950 to 2150 (+10%: the cut cell and the width rule), notifications usage 1050 to 1100 (+5%: the 44px entry on touch). The skip link's rim and radius took the core 30457 to 30609 bytes, under its cap (the rules that hang it under the bar are the topbar module's: 3200 to 3600, +12.5%); core 30720 to 31050 (+1.1%, DECISIONS 147: also the bar's links left out of the rule: the pseudo-element that makes a short standalone link a 44 by 44 target), skip-link script in the topbar module (3200 to 4150 over this PR, +30%: the rules that hang the link under the bar, 3600, and the script that reads the bar's real edge, 4150), sparkline 3600 to 4050 (+12.5%: React's ticker structure, so the value copies once on its line, and in forced colours the strips go and the number is plain text), forms budget 3250 to 3500 (+7.7%: the necessity word), notifications 9050 to 9250 (+2.2%: the 44px entry). Raised in the audit-design-b PR's E2 port (DECISIONS 138 and 139: the core set draws check, close, the chevrons, copy, plus, minus and search wherever a component draws them): the modules that drew a Phosphor icon for one of those now carry the core glyph's whole SVG, written in at build time (`%glyph-svg:name%`, the markup the glyph module's `_.glyph(name)` returns, so no module needs the glyph module and a page pays for nothing it does not use), and the Phosphor path of the same icon leaves the page. Each module's own bytes rose by that markup, and a page's total moved by what the Phosphor path it no longer carries saves: menu 8600 to 8900 (+303), combobox 10900 to 11200 (+303), copy 1900 to 2400 (+640), terminal 8100 to 8850 (+761), toast 13850 to 14150 (+325), number 2900 to 3400 (+557), filter 16400 to 17050 (+785), palette 9900 to 10450 (+536); the command list shares the palette's search drawing and fell 20 bytes. Set in integration-nov15, where the type-layout, motion-rules and audit-design-b branches meet: the combined tree measured SKILL.md 10959 bytes (each side's cap was 10900: both added index lines), core 31192 bytes (caps 30720 and 31050: the page-row and display rules, the three motion tokens and the skip link and 44px target rules all land in the core CSS) and core usage 2348 bytes (caps 2300 and 2250: type-layout's line and the skip-link bullet), so each is set to the measured bytes rounded up to the next 50: skillMd 10900 to 11000, core 31050 to 31200, core usage 2300 to 2350. Raised in the charts port PR (DECISIONS 153, D7a): chart 34400 to 34650 (script 26970 to 27270 bytes, +1.1% on the 34283 it was: `Basalt.trailingMean`, the trend maths React exports as `trailingMean`, 300 bytes), its usage 3150 to 3350 (+6%: one line for it). The tokens the batch adds (chart-lit-top, -mid and -base in both themes, size-chart-plot-sm, size-chart-row, size-meter-marker and radius-2xs) took the art module 2087 to 2546 bytes (budget 2100 to 2600, +24%: the chart tokens are its group) and the core 31192 to 31250 (cap 31200 to 31300, +0.3%: radius-2xs). Only D7a names a skill module in the charts ballot; the lit marks, the headline frame, the phase chart, the share bar, the coverage strip, the marks row and the range meter are React-only in this batch.

textWords: a call to Basalt.kbdGroup or Basalt.hardwareKeyboard
an input of type checkbox or radio (not a choice card's)
a --basalt-art-, --basalt-aspect-, --basalt-chart- or --basalt-size-chart- token, or --basalt-size-stage-headroom (a var() in its own style counts)

a --basalt-text-6xl-, --basalt-text-7xl-, --basalt-text-hero-narrow-, --basalt-text-display-narrow-, --basalt-hero-, --basalt-display-, --basalt-lead- or --basalt-section-gap token, --basalt-space-32, --basalt-size-section-gap or --basalt-size-display-measure (a var() in its own style counts)
a call to Basalt.openPalette or Basalt.closePalette
a call to Basalt.openDialog or Basalt.closeDialog
